picks.headline: Anthropic touts AI-led biology discovery
picks.excerpt: Anthropic says ~950 Claude agent sessions working over 21 hours found ART, a previously unknown CRISPR-like enzyme system with DNA repeat arrays in bacteriophages. The preprint has not been peer-reviewed.
picks.rationale: Agents ran end to end and found a new CRISPR-like system, a notable AI-driven discovery. The copy must say the preprint has not been peer-reviewed. This is a different discovery from the July Anthropic story (MIT TR, 07-15).

picks.headline: New AlphaFold Database release adds viral protein complexes to support pandemic preparedness
picks.excerpt: EMBL-EBI and Google DeepMind, with NVIDIA, Seoul National University and others, added AI-predicted structures for more than 2,800 viruses to the AlphaFold Database to speed up vaccine and diagnostic target discovery.
picks.rationale: A new public resource that researchers can use right away: predicted complexes for 2,800+ viruses. It has a Korean angle (SNU). It is distinct from the 09-07 'AlphaFold limits' story.

picks.headline: AI solves 79-year-old math mystery of six-dimensional spheres
picks.excerpt: Can a six-dimensional sphere be described using imaginary numbers? Experts puzzled over this for decades, and now an AI has apparently answered it.
picks.rationale: A headline math result on a question open since 1947, from a reputable outlet. It is a different problem from the 09-23 M23 inverse-Galois card (SciAm), so it is not a duplicate. Covers mathematics.

picks.headline: AI innovation supports screening for 2.2 million US workers exposed to toxic dust
picks.excerpt: Michigan State University's AI, trained on US worker chest X-rays, detects early pneumoconiosis with 91% accuracy versus 77% for human readers, easing a shortage of about 200 specialist B readers (Occupational and Environmental Medicine).
picks.rationale: A peer-reviewed clinical result with hard numbers (91% vs 77%) and a clear real-world bottleneck (only about 200 B readers). Covers occupational medicine.

picks.headline: Humanoid robots navigate narrow gaps and obstacles with whole-body AI control
picks.excerpt: UC Berkeley and Princeton's TANGO vision-language framework controls all 29 joints of a humanoid from language instructions and camera images. It was trained on 65k synthetic trajectories and doubled success rates over 2D path planning.
picks.rationale: University research with measurable gains (2x success, 29-joint whole-body control). Covers robotics. Chosen over the phage-mutation story to keep Phys.org at 2, and over QC Design Meridian, which is a company self-report.
